[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
'''Peter Glasgow''', also recorded as '''Patrick Glasgow''', was born before October 1762 and baptised on '''10 October 1762''' at West Calder, Midlothian, Scotland. His parents were '''John Glasgow''' and '''Margaret Mill'''.<ref name="Peter1762">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950," database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4T-5P2 : accessed 28 July 2026), Peter Glasgow, baptised 10 October 1762 at West Calder, Midlothian, son of John Glasgow and Margaret Mill; duplicate parent index (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4T-5PL : accessed 28 July 2026), John Glasgow in entry for Peter Glasgow.</ref>

The previous estimate that Peter was born about 1767 should be replaced by the directly recorded 1762 baptism.

Peter later lived at or near Bathgate, Linlithgowshire, where he and '''Elizabeth Dick''' had at least six children between 1783 and 1795.

The baptism of their eldest known child records the father's name as '''Patrick Glasgow'''. The later baptisms record him as '''Peter Glasgow'''. The continuous sequence of children, the same mother and the same parish strongly indicate that Peter and Patrick were the same man.

No marriage record for Peter Glasgow and Elizabeth Dick has yet been identified. Peter's date and place of death remain unknown.

== Research Notes ==
=== Whitebank trial identification — 30 October 2026 ===
The trial index names Peter Glasgow of Whitebank, tried on 9 October 1797. The held memorial transcription for Peter Glasgow-2878 calls him the late tenant of Whitebank, records death on 7 November 1812 aged 72, names Jean Anderson as spouse, and sons John and James as erectors. Matching personal name and the specific tenancy provide a substantially better identification than the Bathgate Peter-1466 comparison, which has no Whitebank link. Prefer Peter-2878 as the trial subject at 94% subjective identity confidence. This is one memorial, also indexed under Jean, not two independent witnesses.

The original memorial image and court papers were not newly inspected. The trial index gives no age, family or occupation; another Peter of the same holding remains possible. The index records a guilty verdict and transportation sentence, not proof of a voyage, destination, actual removal, return or pardon. Do not use this occurrence to infer either man’s parents, alter Peter-1466’s 79% father assessment, or transfer the unassigned 1818 Edinburgh burial. Reassessment of held memorial evidence combined with a fresh index read, not newly discovered court papers.<ref name="WhitebankTrial1797">[https://www.scottishindexes.com/jcdetail.aspx?jcid=1797040&pid=179704079 Scottish Indexes, High Court of Justiciary Trial Papers], Peter Glasgow of Whitebank, 9 October 1797, NRS JC26/1797/40; index checked 30 October 2026. Original court papers not inspected.</ref><ref name="WhitebankMemorial">[https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/198800998/peter_glasgow Peter Glasgow memorial 198800998] and [https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/198800999/jean-glasgow Jean Anderson memorial 198800999], held transcription of one shared Stichill stone, not two witnesses. The stone calls Peter the late tenant of Whitebank; original photograph not newly inspected.</ref>

The Bathgate parent-name variation Patrick/Peter is a real derivative reading, not a corrected transcription: FamilySearch X151-7QY names Patrick Glasgow and Elizabeth Dick for John’s 6 July 1783 baptism. The separate 1762 index VQ4T-5P2 names Peter, John Glasgow and Margaret Mill at West Calder; it does not identify the adult father with the Irvine child. The held 1773 West Calder and 1776 Bathgate John/Margaret Mill child records support a local parental-household comparison but supply no explicit childhood-to-adult bridge. Retain John-3314 as the selected father at 79%; no family or vital field is changed.<ref name="PeterIndexesRechecked">FamilySearch [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4T-5P2 VQ4T-5P2], Peter’s West Calder christening, 10 October 1762, and [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X151-7QY X151-7QY], Patrick in son John’s 1783 Bathgate christening; signed-in index pages read 30 October 2026. === Peter and Patrick ===

The 1783 baptism of John records his father as '''Patrick Glasgow'''. Every later known baptism records the father as '''Peter Glasgow'''.

The records nevertheless form a coherent family:

* the children were recorded at regular intervals between 1783 and 1795;
* the mother was Elizabeth Dick;
* the records belong to the same Bathgate family;
* no competing Patrick Glasgow and Elizabeth Dick family has been identified;
* Peter and Patrick were historically used as interchangeable forenames in Scottish records.

Patrick in the 1783 record should therefore be treated as a variation of Peter rather than evidence that Elizabeth Dick had two husbands.

=== Identification with the West Calder child ===

The adult Peter or Patrick Glasgow of Bathgate is very likely the Peter Glasgow baptised at West Calder in 1762.

The evidence includes:

* Peter was about 20 when his eldest known child was baptised in 1783.
* West Calder and Bathgate are neighbouring parts of the same wider district.
* His father was named John Glasgow.
* Peter named his first known son John.
* His mother was Margaret Mill.
* Peter named a daughter Margaret.
* His probable siblings included Andrew and Agnes.
* Peter later named children Andrew and Agnes.
* No separate adult life has been identified for the Peter baptised at West Calder.

The relationship is strongly supported by chronology, geography and naming patterns, although no marriage or adult record has yet been found explicitly stating that the West Calder child was the husband of Elizabeth Dick.

The strongest points are:

* Peter's first known son was named '''John''', matching Peter's father.
* The name '''Margaret''' appears as both Peter's mother and his daughter.
* The names '''Andrew''' and '''Agnes''' occur among both Peter's probable siblings and his children.

These names were not individually unusual, but the combined repetition supports the identification of the West Calder child with the Bathgate father.

=== Earlier Bathgate comparison to the 1797 trial — superseded preference ===

A '''Peter Glasgow of Whitebank''' was tried before the High Court of Justiciary on 9 October 1797 for rioting.<ref name="Trial1797">"High Court of Justiciary Trial Papers," index, Scottish Indexes (https://www.scottishindexes.com/jcdetail.aspx?jcid=1797040&pid=179704079 : accessed 28 July 2026), Peter Glasgow of Whitebank, accused of rioting, tried 9 October 1797; citing National Records of Scotland, JC26/1797/40.</ref>

The trial papers also relate to Robert Lillie, blacksmith in Haddington; Christopher Kerr of Bankhead; James Richardson of Crooklaw; and Elizabeth Wilson of Dunse.<ref name="Trial1797"/>

This Peter may have been the husband of Elizabeth Dick, but the identification is not proved.

'''Reasons the identification is plausible:'''

* Peter would have been about 35 in 1797.
* His last currently known child was baptised in 1795.
* No later baptism or death record has yet been securely identified for him.
* A sentence of transportation could explain his disappearance from later Scottish records.

'''Reasons for caution:'''

* The trial index gives no age, birthplace, occupation, spouse or relatives.
* The designation Whitebank has not yet been connected to Peter's Bathgate family.
* The other accused were associated with Haddington, Bankhead, Crooklaw and Dunse, whereas Peter's documented family was centred on West Calder and Bathgate.
* A sentence of transportation does not itself prove that the sentence was carried out.
* Another man of the same name could have been involved.

The 1797 prosecution should remain recorded as a possible event until the original trial papers, precognition and court minutes provide enough identifying information.

=== Possible identity of Peter's father ===

The John Glasgow who married or partnered with Margaret Mill is represented by the FamilySearch profile:

* [https://www.familysearch.org/en/tree/person/9Q1F-9BL John Glasgow, FamilySearch ID 9Q1F-9BL]

A leading working hypothesis identifies him with '''John Glasgow baptised on 28 March 1740 at Irvine, Ayrshire''', son of [[Glasgow-1058|George Glasgow]] and [[Martin-103040|Margaret Martin]].

That identification is supported by:

* John's suitable age to father Peter in 1762;
* the recurrence of Andrew, Margaret and Agnes in following generations;
* the wider family's movement through Ayrshire, Edinburgh, West Calder and Bathgate;
* the absence of another known wife or family for the Irvine-born John;
* an existing association between the wider Glasgow family and women surnamed Mill.

It remains unproved. No record has yet been found explicitly identifying the Irvine-born John as Margaret Mill's husband.

=== Son John and the Canongate family ===

Peter and Elizabeth's eldest known son, John Glasgow, was reportedly born on 7 June 1783 and baptised at Bathgate on 6 July 1783.<ref name="John1783"/>

He is probably the John Glasgow who later lived with Jean Bryce at Hume's Close, Canongate, Edinburgh, and worked as a shop porter.

Evidence supporting that identification includes:

* the age is within one year of the age recorded in 1841;
* Bathgate was outside Midlothian, matching the census response;
* Peter, John, Margaret, Elizabeth and William recur in both families;
* the family followed a plausible West Calder–Bathgate–Canongate migration route;
* John's probable sister Elizabeth is reported to have married at Canongate in 1809.

The identification remains circumstantial because no adult record explicitly states that the Bathgate-born John became the Canongate porter.

=== Unresolved 1800 marriage entry ===

A marriage index dated 1800 associates a woman surnamed Glasgow with Alexander Hunter.<ref name="Hunter1800">"Scotland, Marriages, 1561–1910," database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYSW-FB4 : accessed 28 July 2026), Glasgow in entry for Alexander Hunter, 1800.</ref>

The supplied extract does not show the woman's forename. She may have been one of Peter's sisters, but the record should not be assigned until the complete entry is examined.

=== Research priorities ===

* Obtain the original West Calder baptism of Peter dated 10 October 1762.
* Find the marriage or proclamation of Peter or Patrick Glasgow and Elizabeth Dick.
* Examine the original Bathgate baptisms for the parents' residence, occupation and witnesses.
* Obtain the original trial papers and court minutes for NRS reference JC26/1797/40.
* Determine whether the 1797 transportation sentence was carried out and identify the destination.
* Compare the trial papers' age, occupation, residence and relatives with the Bathgate Peter.
* Determine the parents of Elizabeth Dick.
* Trace Peter through tax records, kirk-session minutes, testaments, land records and burial registers.
* Examine the original baptisms of Peter's probable siblings to confirm Margaret Mill as their mother.
* Find the marriage or proclamation of John Glasgow and Margaret Mill.
* Test whether Peter's father was the John Glasgow baptised at Irvine in 1740.
* Treat the 1797 criminal record and the line beyond John Glasgow and Margaret Mill as hypotheses until supported by direct evidence.
